newsitem.title: GERMANY: German communities fight Bonn's energy reforms.
newsitem.headline: German communities fight Bonn's energy reforms.

text.p: Local German governments are challenging federal efforts to eliminate regional monopolies in electricity and gas markets, saying they would disrupt the localities' fiscal and environmental policies.
In a meeting with Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt on Tuesday, local governments warned against the proposed legal changes, which Rexrodt has vowed to carry out this month.

Rexrodt told journalists after the meeting that the new draft law contained provisions that would allow local governments to continue collecting revenues from utilities, but that the localities harboured doubts.
European Union energy ministers agreed in June to encourage competition in electricity and gas markets, and Germany is now trying to set the legal framework for the change.
Major German utilities pay local authorities for the right to deliver gas and electricity in certain areas, and the local authorities themselves operate utilities in some places.

Joerg Hennerkes, a spokesman for the German Association of Cities and Localities, said financing for public transportation could be in danger, and increased competition could make it harder to promote environmentally friendly energy sources.

Association president Gerhard Seiler said the councils approved of the EU's move to gradually eliminate electricity monopolies, and would be interested in becoming "single buyers" for their communities.
But Rexrodt is intent on his principle of "negotiated third-party access", which will allow major customers to haggle over electricity rates with their utilities.
Rexrodt said the new law would give localities the opportunity to cut costs through shrewd purchasing, but that the communities would also have to rationalise.
Federal and local authorities agreed that water should not be subject to the proposed legislative changes.
